# Exporting and Reproducible Figure Workflows

:::cdi-message
- **ID:** VISPY-009
- **Type:** Lesson
- **Audience:** Public
- **Theme:** Reproducible figure export and publication discipline
:::

Professional visualization is not only about creating figures.
It is about exporting them consistently and reproducibly.

In this lesson you will:

- understand static vs interactive outputs
- export high-resolution PNG figures
- control figure dimensions
- maintain clean project structure
- avoid duplicate or unstable outputs in Quarto builds

All figures are exported to `figures/` using CDI helpers.

---

## Setup

```{python}
import warnings
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import plotly.express as px

from cdi_viz.theme import (
    cdi_notebook_init,
    cdi_theme,
    show_and_save_mpl,
    show_and_save_plotly,
)

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

cdi_notebook_init(chapter="09")

df = pd.read_csv("data/cdi-student-outcomes.csv")

print("First rows:")
print(df.head())
```

---

## Static Export: Matplotlib (High Resolution)

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.6))

ax.scatter(df["study_hours"], df["math_score"], alpha=0.6)

ax.set_title("Study hours vs math score")
ax.set_xlabel("Study hours per week")
ax.set_ylabel("Math score")

fig.tight_layout()

show_and_save_mpl(fig, dpi=300)  # figures/09_001.png
```

---

## Controlling Figure Size

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))

sns.histplot(df["math_score"], bins=25, ax=ax)

ax.set_title("Distribution of math scores")
ax.set_xlabel("Math score")
ax.set_ylabel("Count")

fig.tight_layout()

show_and_save_mpl(fig, dpi=300)  # figures/09_002.png
```

---

## Plotly: Static Snapshot Export

```{python}
fig = px.scatter(
    df,
    x="study_hours",
    y="math_score",
    color="test_prep",
    title="Study hours vs math score (Plotly)",
)

cdi_theme(fig)

show_and_save_plotly(fig, show=False)  # figures/09_003.png
```

---

## Project Structure Discipline

A clean visualization project should look like this:

project-root/
│
├── data/
├── figures/
├── cdi_viz/
├── 01-preface-and-setup.qmd
├── 02-story-driven-visualization.qmd
...

Rules:

- Never manually rename exported figures
- Let the chapter counter manage numbering
- Keep figure filenames deterministic

---

## Key Takeaways

- Professional visualization requires export discipline.
- Use consistent figure sizes.
- Control DPI intentionally.
- Keep project structure clean.
- Use CDI helpers to standardize outputs.

3. Create a Plotly histogram and export a static snapshot.
4. Inspect your `figures/` folder and confirm numbering consistency.
